question: What is the meaning of nanoplastic release in relation to product environmental footprint?
description: Nanoplastic release in relation to product environmental footprint refers to the release of extremely small plastic particles during various stages of the product's life cycle, such as manufacturing, transport, use, and end-of-life. This aspect is significant as it contributes to the overall environmental impact of the product, particularly in terms of pollution and potential harm to ecosystems.

references.text:
(n) the carbon footprint of the product;
(o) the material footprint of the product;
(p) microplastic and nanoplastic release as expressed through the release during relevant product life cycle stages, 
including manufacturing, transport, use and end-of-life stages;
(q) emissions to air, water or soil released in one or more lifecycle stages of the product as expressed through quantities 
and nature of emissions, including noise;
(r)
amounts of waste generated, including plastic waste and packaging waste and their ease of reuse, and amounts of 
hazardous waste generated;
(s)
functional performance and conditions for use, including as expressed through the ability to perform its intended use, 
precautions for use, skills required and compatibility with other products or systems;
(t)
lightweight design as expressed through reduction of material consumption, load- and stress-optimisation of 
structures, integration of functions within the material or into a single product component, use of lower density or 
high-strength materials and hybrid materials, with regard to material savings, recycling and other circularity aspects, 
and waste reduction.
